Core Active Vocabulary (5 items):

speak — to say words. Example: I can speak Spanish.
read — to look at words and understand them. Example: I can read French.
write — to make words with a pen. Example: I can't write Chinese.
listen — to pay attention to sound. Example: I listen to the radio.
understand — to know what words mean. Example: I understand Italian a little.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• I can speak ...
• I can't write ...
• Can you understand ...?
• I can read a little.
• Yes, I can. / No, I can't.
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'to say words'?
Which word means 'to look at words and understand them'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
can is weak /kən/ in statements and strong /kæn/ in short answers.
I can /kən/ speak. Yes, I can /kæn/.
Listen and repeat three times.
Which word carries the main stress?
Grammar focus: Can / Can't for language ability.
Use can + verb for language ability: I can speak English. I can't write Chinese. Use read, write, listen and understand as separate skills: I can read but I can't speak well.
Controlled practice: choose the correct option.

Choose the correct negative.
